summary: Microsoft's MAI-Code-1-Flash card describes a text-only sparse-MoE coding model for Copilot developer workflows. It reports production-harness coding, reasoning, instruction-following, and tool-use benchmarks, while safety discussion stays qualitative and the model is now retired in the GitHub catalog.

capabilities.text: Text-to-text coding model with a 256K-token context and sparse-MoE transformer architecture.
Targets agentic coding, repository Q&A, refactoring, completion, and tool-using Copilot workflows.
Training includes supervised tuning, a synthetic agentic phase with about 2 million tasks, and reinforcement learning over more than 150,000 environments.
Validated in the GitHub Copilot production harness on software-engineering, repository Q&A, refactoring, and usage-derived tasks.

safety_findings.text: Harmful content is filtered or down-ranked during pretraining.
Alignment work during supervised tuning and reinforcement learning is used to discourage unsafe outputs.
CyberBench, CyberSecEval, and SecRepo are named as cybersecurity and secure-coding evaluations.
The release process used safety classifiers and filters around production APIs.

limitations.text: The GitHub catalog marks the model retired as of 2026-09-10.
The card lists text input only, so it does not document image-grounded behavior.
The initial distribution section was limited to Visual Studio Code with CLI planned later.
Safety results are described qualitatively without benchmark pass rates.
Generated output can be faulty and requires review and validation.

practical_implications.text: GitHub retired the model on 2026-09-10; remaining guidance is historical and useful for successor comparison.
Use MAI-Code-1-Flash as the baseline when interpreting MAI-Code-1.1-Flash improvements.
Rely on tests and code review rather than benchmark scores when judging old generated changes.
Do not infer image-input behavior from this card.
Treat historical availability notes as stale unless confirmed in current Copilot docs.

coverage_notes: This digest summarizes the complete six-page MAI-Code-1-Flash card and avoids administrative contact details. It treats the model as retired in the catalog and does not apply later MAI-Code-1.1-Flash capabilities retroactively.
